item.title: Families of USS Lincoln crew say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board
item.description: President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.
item.content:encoded:
President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.

(Image credit: Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

item.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, is found dead
item.description: Arday was 37 when he became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023. He was found unresponsive Friday at a home in southwest London.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: They fought for the U.S. in Afghanistan. Now they worry about losing their green cards
item.description: When the U.S. withdrew from Afghanistan five years ago, thousands of Afghans who helped U.S. troops were brought here to rebuild their lives. But now, some fear the U.S. may want to send them back.

item.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia's coast, killing at least 38
item.description: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early Saturday, killing at least 38 people, collapsing buildings as well as causing panic in a region prone to deadly quakes.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The Taliban has taken a terrible toll on the education of girls -- and boys as well
item.description: Saturday marks the 5th anniversary of the current Taliban rule in Afghanistan. They've had a devastating impact on girls' education. A lesser told story is their impact on the education of boys.

item.title: Feds probe 'mention markets.' And, lawmakers call for investigation into USS Lincoln

item.title: From Europe to Asia, floods to heatwaves, world experiences weather shocks
item.description: At least eight people died in Japan as heavy rains flooded roads and disrupted traffic while firefighters from Britain to France and Croatia struggled to contain blazes in Europe's fifth heatwave this summer
